title: U.S. House · Colorado's 1st District

context.text: This is an open seat: Melat Kiros defeated incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette and Wanda James 53.2%-39.8%-7.0% in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, so DeGette will not appear on the November ballot. Christy Peterson advanced unopposed from the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Melat Kiros
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette

summary.text: Melat Kiros is a Denver attorney who defeated incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette in the Democratic primary for Colorado's 1st Congressional District. She immigrated to the U.S. from Tigray, Ethiopia in 1998.

background.text: Immigrated to Denver, Colorado, from Tigray, Ethiopia, in 1998 with her family.
Earned bachelor's degrees in Political Science and Economics from Washington College (2018) and a law degree from the University of Notre Dame (2022).
Career experience includes working as a lawyer and, earlier, as a barista.

priorities.text: Campaign finance and lobbying reform, plus congressional term limits, to reduce the influence of money in politics.
Expanding voting rights and consolidating elections into a single day with a shorter election cycle.
Codifying access to housing, health care, nutritious food and public education as basic needs for every American.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will always stand for Medicare for All and describes health care access as directly linked to life expectancy and economic outcomes.
Campaign platform frames housing as a basic human right and calls for a 'Housing First' approach, without specifying rent-regulation policy in detail.
Says she will always stand for universal childcare as part of putting working families first.
Campaign website calls for an arms embargo and says tax dollars should not support what she describes as a genocide, opposing continued unconditional military aid.

summary.text: Christy Peterson is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 1st Congressional District. She works in accounting and describes her candidacy as focused on public safety and reducing government spending in Denver.

background.text: Graduated from Chatfield Senior High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from San Diego State University in 2006.
Career experience includes working in accounting/office management in construction; states she is pursuing a doctorate in natural and functional medicine.

priorities.text: Public safety: says reducing crime and 'soft on crime' policies in Denver is her top priority, arguing this would let businesses and visitors return to the city.
Reducing government waste, fraud and abuse, and creating incentives for business growth and job creation.

positions.summary: Says making cities safe again is her top priority and that crime and lax enforcement have driven residents and businesses away.
Campaign survey lists opposition to costs she associates with unauthorized immigration among her stated concerns for the district.
States support for protecting the right to bear arms in her Ballotpedia survey response.
